task.title: Card-detail Back walks printing flips instead of leaving the page
task.description:
Maintainer report (2026-08-16, desktop .app): the card-detail Back control doesn't return to the page the card was clicked from — it only steps back through card printings when several were viewed. Mechanism (verify): #158 made each printings-row click navigate to ?printing=<id> as a PUSHED history entry, and #156's Back pops history one entry at a time — so every printing flip becomes a back-target and Back unwinds them before ever leaving the page. Also check whether anything pushes a printing param on initial load (which would make even a no-flip visit need two Backs).

Fix per existing policy ('history granularity is per session', the rule #156 recorded for ?q= edits): printing switches within one card visit REPLACE the history entry instead of pushing — the whole card visit stays one back-target, Back always leaves to the source page. Audit every ?printing= navigation source: the printings-table stretched row links, CardPreview's detail_href override on that page, and any programmatic printing selection. Leptos router: row links may need navigate-with-replace instead of plain <a> push semantics — follow however the app already does replace-navigations (catalog QueryBar precedent).

Verify: e2e in card-detail.spec.ts — (a) catalog → card → Back lands on the same catalog URL (exists from #156, must stay green); (b) NEW: catalog → card → flip 2 printings → ONE Back returns to catalog (would fail today); (c) #158's printing-navigation tests updated for replace semantics (URL still shows ?printing= and reorders — only the history behavior changes); (d) #156's double-back-from-entry test stays green. The history-stamping wrapper treats replaceState as carrying the current entry's marker — confirm a replaced printing param doesn't corrupt has_history.
